edits.ptolemy-rare-male:
Use case: precise-object-edit / identity-preserving anatomical correction. Image1 is the edit target, an existing Everfolk historical card inner painting. Image2 is an authentic modern furniture-maker photograph used ONLY for natural neck/shoulder connection and downward work-focused gaze; do not copy the photographed face, clothing, background or tools. Make a tightly localized correction to the painted official's HEAD, NECK and immediate collar only. Replace the strained extreme LEFTWARD profile with a natural forward/downward three-quarter head aligned with the torso. The face should nod gently toward the foreground grain sack and clay seal beneath the official's right hand, with visible pupils unambiguously focused on this inspection task. The head rests centrally over the collar, neck short and relaxed with natural sternocleidomastoid/trapezius connections; avoid stretched neck cords, sideways bending, a floating head, chin forced against shoulder or looking out of the left edge. Preserve the character's recognizable adult face, age, Mediterranean appearance and hairstyle. Keep the existing shoulders and body orientation fixed. Preserve BOTH hands and every finger, raised wooden tablet, grain sack, clay seal, scales, wheat/grain, ropes, garments below the collar, background workers, river boat, architecture, sunset, painterly brushwork, lighting and full canvas composition. Do not change the work props, move the arms or recompose the scene. Output one complete painting at the same dimensions and portrait 4:5 composition as Image1, no photo insert, no split screen, no frame, no labels, no watermark. The intended result is the same commissioner now calmly checking the work directly in front of them.
Variant: adult man; retain short dark curly hair, original masculine face, clean-shaven appearance.
